contributions.text: 12. What progress her Department has made on the Mission Coastal programme.
contributions.name: Alison Hume

contributions.who: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education (Josh MacAlister)
contributions.text: As a coastal MP, I recognise the significant challenges faced by many coastal communities. That is why we are making progress on Mission Coastal, and why it is so important. I know that the Minister for School Standards was delighted to join the Scarborough and Whitby team for Mission Coastal recently to progress the plans.
contributions.name: Josh MacAlister
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education

contributions.text: Mission Coastal is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to improve educational outcomes for children in Scarborough and Whitby. More than 24% of pupils in my constituency are persistently out of school. Does the Minister agree with me that addressing the reasons for that has to be the starting point for Mission Coastal?
contributions.name: Alison Hume

contributions.text: My hon. Friend is absolutely right to raise the issue of persistent absence. Since the election, this Government have made real progress on the issue nationally; 115,000 fewer children have been persistently absent since we came to power. However, there are areas in our country where the issue is deeper. The approach we are taking with Mission Coastal brings partners together at a local level, so that there is learning not just from the top down, but from the ground back up to Government, and we can make the changes needed to ensure that every child gets to school when they need to be there.
contributions.name: Josh MacAlister
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Education
